messages:
maya: Quick question — hit a weird precedence case in prod. org-level flag `enable_new_routing` is ON. project `search` has a canary audience that should get the new routing, but the route `/api/search/embed` has a route-level override set to FORCE_OFF for that feature. In prod the embed route still seems to be getting canary traffic (only when model=embed-v2). Which should win in our resolution? Do audience predicates get evaluated after route-level short-circuit?

sam: Short answer: route-level explicit toggles should short-circuit and win. Audience/canary checks belong to project-scope evaluation, which is lower priority. But there are historical caveats — audience predicates can reference model/route attrs and some eval paths were running predicates at a later stage. I'll paste the eval order I think we use.

sam: ```
resolution_order (rough):
1) explicit route flags (force_on / force_off)
2) model-specific overrides (per-model config)
3) project-level flags (includes audience-based canaries)
4) org defaults
```

liam: That matches the flagstore docs, but note: we've seen a bug where audience predicates were evaluated inside the model-selection step, which allowed a predicate to re-enable the feature for a specific model even when route had force_off earlier. Result: route force_off didn't feel absolute.

olga: Do we have a unit/integration test covering route+project+audience+model combos? We should add one that asserts route.force_off always wins.

maya: I have a user repro and trace: https://go/trace/XYZ123 (link). Embeddings route (/api/search/embed) got canary for embed-v2 users; search route (/api/search) did not. Sounds consistent with the eval-bug theory.

sam: Thanks @maya. Can you attach the trace to the GH issue? I'll draft a small fix. In the meantime we should pause the search canary rollout until we confirm. @eng-oncall FYI.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout `search-canary-v2` scheduled; started at 1759995588; currently 5% traffic to dedicated pool.

liam: If the intended semantics are that route overrides are authoritative, we should enforce route-level checks earlier in the request pipeline (pre-audience-eval). I can open a PR that moves the check and adds a lint to catch regressions.

olga: +1 to that PR. Also propose we add a short playbook note: `Route overrides are authoritative unless an explicit opt-in to audience-level override is documented and reviewed.` Saves follow-up confusion.

maya: Sounds good. @sam please assign the GH issue to me so I can add the failing test and attach the trace. I'll also add a minimal integration test that simulates route+model+audience combos.

sam: Will do. I'll create PR #12345 with the evaluation order change and tests, and reference this thread.

maya: Blocking the rollout until PR merges and CI passes. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks all — I'll ping here when the PR is ready for review.
